meta.title: Tree India Foundation | Transforming Roots through Ecology & Education
meta.desc: Tree India Foundation (TIF) is a registered environmental non-profit restoring forests, greening schools, and building community stewardship across Maharashtra, India.

about.title: A grassroots foundation for a greener, more accountable India
about.intro: Tree India Foundation (TIF) is a registered non-profit working at the meeting point of ecology and education, planting forests that survive, and raising a generation that keeps them growing.
about.p1: We believe reforestation only lasts when communities own it. So our work pairs native-species plantation with hands-on environmental learning in schools and villages, building the skills, habits, and local leadership that keep green cover alive long after the saplings go in.
about.p2: From the dense Miyawaki groves we grow on small plots, to the Green Skill Labs and Eco Cabinets we set up in classrooms, every programme is measured, monitored, and reported, because a promise to plant should come with proof it took root.
about.vision.b: An India where every community protects its own green cover, and every child grows up an ecological steward.
about.mission.b: To restore native ecosystems and embed environmental education across schools and communities, transparently, measurably, and at scale.
pillar.1.d: Native, Miyawaki-method forests that regenerate fast and survive.
pillar.2.d: NEP 2020-aligned, experiential eco-literacy for every classroom.
pillar.3.d: Village-led plantation and stewardship, aligned with CAMPA.
pillar.4.d: Transparent monitoring, survival tracking, and CSR/BRSR-ready reporting.
work.title: Programmes that plant, teach, and last
work.intro: Each initiative connects ecology with education, turning plantation into a lived, measured practice for schools and communities.
prog.1.d: Dense, fast-growing native forests on small urban and rural plots, designed to become self-sustaining within a few years.
prog.2.d: An NEP 2020 experiential-learning model with Green Skill Labs, Eco Cabinets, and student Green Ambassadors leading eco-action on campus.
prog.3.d: Annual tree-planting festivals that bring villages, schools, and volunteers together to green shared public land.
prog.4.d: Curriculum-linked eco-literacy, teacher training, and student workbooks that make sustainability a habit, not a topic.
prog.5.d: Working with gram panchayats and forest-fringe communities on CAMPA-aligned plantation and long-term local ownership.
prog.6.d: Geo-tagged plantation records, sapling survival audits, and CSR/BRSR-ready impact reports, so every contribution is traceable.

inv.title: Three ways to help India grow greener
inv.intro: Whether you have time, a school, or a CSR budget, there's a place for you in this work.
inv.1.d: Join plantation drives, mentor Green Ambassadors, or lend your skills to a programme near you.
inv.2.d: Schools, gram panchayats, and institutions: bring the Green School model or a plantation project to your community.
inv.3.d: Support Schedule VII-eligible, CSR/BRSR-ready projects with transparent, geo-tagged reporting on every rupee.
